title: Algebraic residue extensions over closed base points give closed scheme points
statement: Let $f:Y\to S$ be any morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $y\in Y$, and put $s=f(y)$. Use the induced residue-field homomorphism $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(y)$ [def-weil-residue-field]. Suppose that $\{s\}$ is closed in $S$ and that this field extension is algebraic, meaning that each element of $\kappa(y)$ is a root of a nonzero polynomial over $\kappa(s)$ [def-weil-algebraic-element, def-pc-field-extension]. Then $\{y\}$ is closed in $Y$. No local finite-type, quasi-compactness, separatedness, or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Let $z\in\overline{\{y\}}$. Continuity gives $f(z)\in\overline{\{s\}}=\{s\}$. Choose an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ about $s$, and then an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ about $z$ contained in $f^{-1}V$, using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] twice. Every open neighbourhood of $z$ contains $y$, so $y\in U$. By [def-weil-affine-spectrum], the restriction $U\to V$ comes from a ring map $A\to B$. Write $\mathfrak p\subset A$ for $s$, $\mathfrak q\subset B$ for $y$, and $\mathfrak r\subset B$ for $z$.

source.place: Tag 01TE (lemma-algebraic-residue-field-extension-closed-point-fibre), affine-open argument; Tag 01IT (lemma-basis-affine-opens). We work in charts about an arbitrary specialization instead of first forming the fibre.

proof.text: The singleton $\{\mathfrak p\}$ is closed in $V$. The closure formula of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes] gives $V(\mathfrak p)=\{\mathfrak p\}$. Choose a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\supseteq\mathfrak p$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal]; then $\mathfrak m\in V(\mathfrak p)$, so $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak p$. Thus $A/\mathfrak p$ is a field. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-field-point-residue-field], $\kappa(s)=\operatorname{Frac}(A/\mathfrak p)=A/\mathfrak p$, and $B/\mathfrak q$ embeds in $\kappa(y)$. The map $A\to B/\mathfrak q$ has kernel $\mathfrak p$, since the image of $y$ is $s$. Hence it embeds $k=A/\mathfrak p$ in $C=B/\mathfrak q$. By the definition of the induced residue map [def-weil-residue-field], these embeddings give $k\subseteq C\subseteq\kappa(y)$ with exactly the specified structural map $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(y)$: all three maps are induced by the section maps followed by germs and residue quotients.

source.place: Tag 00GA (lemma-finite-residue-extension-closed), proof diagram; Tag 00ES (lemma-irreducible), part (1), and Tag 00E0 (lemma-Zariski-topology), maximal-ideal existence.

proof.text:
Here is the elementary field argument in the proof of Tag 00GA, written out rather than made a new node. For $0
e b\in C$, algebraicity [def-weil-algebraic-element] gives a nonzero polynomial relation over $k$. Delete its initial zero coefficients by dividing out a power of $b$ in $\kappa(y)$; this gives $a_0+a_1b+\cdots+a_nb^n=0$ with $a_0
e0$. Since $k$ is a field, $b^{-1}=-a_0^{-1}(a_1+\cdots+a_nb^{n-1})\in C$. Thus $C$ is a field. Consequently $\mathfrak q$ is maximal: an ideal strictly containing $\mathfrak q$ contains some $c
otin\mathfrak q$; lifting the inverse of its nonzero class in $C$ shows that ideal contains $1$.

source.place: Tag 0BID (lemma-subalgebra-algebraic-extension-field), proof (the inverse-polynomial formula), used in Algebra Tag 00GA.

proof.text: Since $U$ is open and contains both points, $z\in\overline{\{y\}}$ also holds in $U$. By the closure formula and inclusion criterion in [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes], $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak r$. Maximality of $\mathfrak q$ and properness of the prime $\mathfrak r$ give $\mathfrak r=\mathfrak q$, hence $z=y$. Every point of $\overline{\{y\}}$ is therefore $y$, so this closure is $\{y\}$ and $\{y\}$ is closed in $Y$.
